title.rendered: I Am Redeemed Through His Blood: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of sins, in accordance with the riches of God’s grace lavished on us. Not partial redemption. Not provisional forgiveness. Bought, washed, and brought home.

content.rendered:
In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of sins, in accordance with the riches of God’s grace. Not partial redemption. Not provisional forgiveness. In Him, you have been bought back, washed clean, and brought home.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, July 5, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, in accordance with the riches of God’s grace that he lavished on us.”
Ephesians 1:7-8 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Paul continues building the great identity statement of Ephesians 1. Yesterday we saw that we were chosen before the foundation of the world. Today we see what that choice cost. Not just a divine decree from a distant throne. Blood. The blood of the Son of God. The Father’s choice of the believer was so determined that He sent His own Son to the cross to make it possible. The redemption is not theoretical. The redemption is bought and paid for in the most precious currency in the universe.

The Greek word for “redemption” is apolutrōsis. In the first century, it was the word used for the buying back of a slave. A slave in the Roman world could be redeemed if someone paid the ransom price to the slave owner. The slave would then walk out of the household as a free person, the property of the redeemer rather than of the old master. Paul says this is exactly what has happened in Christ. The believer was a slave to sin. Christ paid the ransom price with His own blood. The believer now walks free, belonging to Christ rather than to sin.

And Paul places the redemption in the context of forgiveness. The Greek word for “forgiveness” is aphesis. It means a release, a sending away, a complete dismissal. The sins are not just covered. They are sent away. They are released from the believer’s account. They are gone, in the legal and spiritual sense, never to return. This is not a partial pardon. It is a total dismissal of the debt that was against us.

And Paul piles on the language to make sure we get the scale of it. Not just grace. The riches of God’s grace. Not just measured out. Lavished on us. The Greek word is perisseuō, to abound, to overflow, to be more than enough. The Father did not measure His grace out in careful spoonfuls. He poured it over the believer in lavish, abundant, overflowing supply. The grace is not running low. It cannot run low. It is the inexhaustible riches of God.

For Gospelbuzz readers, Sunday is a fitting day for this truth to land. Today, in churches across the world, believers will gather to remember what was accomplished at the cross. The bread will be broken. The cup will be raised. The blood of Jesus will be named again as the price of our redemption. The forgiveness will be celebrated as the lavish gift of a Father who has poured out the riches of His grace on us. Walk into worship today as the redeemed of the Lord. The price has been paid. The forgiveness is yours. The grace is enough.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that I am redeemed through the blood of Jesus. The price has been paid. My sins are forgiven, sent away, released from my account in accordance with the riches of Your grace lavished on me in Christ. I am no longer a slave. I belong to You. The blood of Jesus has settled my redemption forever. I walk in this redemption today, free, forgiven, and lavished upon by Your grace. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am redeemed through the blood of Jesus. My sins are forgiven. The riches of God’s grace have been lavished on me. I belong to Christ.
